title: _enrich_single_table returns matched=True while status='unmatched_value', so a value the trace cannot attribute to any entry or the default is still flagged as a match
description: The returned `matched` field (line 177: `matched and not default_used`, where `matched = rate_value is not None`) is derived purely from value-presence, but `status` (lines 161-168) is derived from `matched_entry is not None`. These diverge for the `unmatched_value` branch: when the rating join produced a NON-null `rate_value` that (a) Python's `normalise_rating_key` walk could not attribute to any `entries` row AND (b) does not equal a usable finite `default_val`, the code sets status='unmatched_value' yet matched=True (and default_used=False). The frontend warning-chip contract relies on `matched`/`default_used` to flag suspicious rows (cf. tests/test_optimiser_apply_trace_enrichment.py:450-451 'frontend warning-chip contract'), so an unattributable value — exactly the suspicious case — is hidden behind matched=True. The single-table convenience path propagates this upward: enrich_rating_step sets result['matched']=t['matched'] (line 248), and the multi-table path ORs t['matched'] (line 256), so the top-level rating detail also reports matched=True for an unmatched_value row. Reachable cases: (1) the documented Float32 non-integer factor-key gap (normalise_rating_key docstring at src/haute/_rating.py:329-333 explicitly excludes non-integer Float32 columns from the engine-agreement guarantee — the engine matches an entry and fills its value, but normalise_rating_key formats the float differently and finds no entry); (2) a non-finite/non-numeric configured defaultValue that the engine nonetheless used (e.g. defaultValue='inf' => default_val=None at lines 132-133 => default_used can never become True at line 155, so a real defaulted miss with a non-null fill becomes status='unmatched_value', matched=True).
evidence: Trace for defaultValue='inf', input miss, engine fills a non-null value v: line 127 has_default truthy; line 129 default_val=float('inf'); line 132 not isfinite => default_val=None. matched_entry stays None (no entry matched / or miss). line 153 matched = (v is not None) = True. line 155 guard `default_val is not None` is False => default_used stays False. Status ladder: not default_used, matched_entry is None, rate_value is not None => line 168 status='unmatched_value'. Return line 177: `matched and not default_used` = True. => {status:'unmatched_value', matched:True, default_used:False}. The existing test test_default_value_infinity (tests/test_trace_enrichment.py:3260) only asserts default_value is None and uses a value (0.5) that isn't the inf fill, so it never checks matched/status for an actually-used non-finite default. The engine-agreement harness assert_engine_and_enrichment_agree (tests/test_rating_key_agreement.py:565-577) only ever asserts the matched/default/no_match trichotomy and has no branch for 'unmatched_value', so this internally-inconsistent state is entirely unguarded.
